LevelOfDistribution

level of distribution: Bombieri-Vinogradov and the Elliott-Halberstam conjecture
Planned: citation of a published resultring 1Primes in the columns of large cycles: level of distribution and Elliott-Halberstam

Fix a largest number. For every width up to a top width, lay the numbers out in rows of that width, compare each survivor column's prime count with its fair share, and keep the worst miss; add the worst misses over all widths. The primes have a level of distribution at a power of the largest number if that total is smaller than the prime count divided by any fixed power of its logarithm, with the top width that power of the largest number. Bombieri-Vinogradov proves the level one half (cited); the Elliott-Halberstam conjecture claims every level below one (an open hypothesis, never claimed); Friedlander and Granville showed the full width fails (cited). Also recorded: the best results past one half for a single chosen column with weighted widths (cited), what Elliott-Halberstam would give for prime gaps (cited), and Bombieri's result that even the full conjecture leaves the sieve unable to tell primes from products of two primes (cited).

Open conjectures it assumes (never claimed): elliott_halberstam

Rests on

No other node: Mathlib and the shared vocabulary only.

Published sources

  • Elliott-Halberstam conjecture (Wikipedia) — states the conjecture (P. D. T. A. Elliott and H. Halberstam, Symposia Mathematica 4, 1970) and summarises what is known
  • Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem (Wikipedia) — states the level one half (E. Bombieri, On the large sieve, Mathematika 12 (1965); A. I. Vinogradov, 1965)
  • J. Friedlander and A. Granville, Limitations to the equi-distribution of primes I, Ann. of Math. 129 (1989), 363-382 — shows the conjecture fails at the full width; cited as friedlander_granville
  • E. Bombieri, J. Friedlander and H. Iwaniec, Primes in arithmetic progressions to large moduli, Acta Math. 156 (1986), 203-251 — first fixed-column level past one half (4/7, well-factorable weights)
  • J. Maynard, Primes in arithmetic progressions to large moduli II: well-factorable estimates, arXiv 2006.07088 — fixed-column level 3/5
  • J. D. Lichtman, Primes in arithmetic progressions to large moduli, and Goldbach beyond the square-root barrier, arXiv 2309.08522 — fixed-column level 66/107, triply well-factorable weights
  • A. Pascadi, On the exponents of distribution of primes and smooth numbers, arXiv 2505.00653 — fixed-column level 5/8, triply well-factorable weights, unconditionally; the current record cited as fixed_column_level
  • D. A. Goldston, J. Pintz and C. Y. Yıldırım, Primes in tuples I, Ann. of Math. 170 (2009), arXiv math/0508185 — any level past one half gives bounded prime gaps
  • J. Maynard, Small gaps between primes, Ann. of Math. 181 (2015), arXiv 1311.4600 — on Elliott-Halberstam, gaps of at most 12 infinitely often; cited as eh_bounded_gaps
  • D. H. J. Polymath, Variants of the Selberg sieve, and bounded intervals containing many primes, arXiv 1407.4897 — on the generalized Elliott-Halberstam conjecture, gaps of at most 6; cited as geh_bounded_gaps
  • K. Ford, On Bombieri's asymptotic sieve, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 357 (2005), 1663-1674 — explains Bombieri's asymptotic sieve (1976): even the full conjecture does not let a sieve separate primes from products of two primes; cited as bombieri_asymptotic_sieve

Related nodes

Connected in content but not by an arrow; each entry says how.

  • ProgressionPNT the one-width form, as the rows go on; this node asks for all widths at once up to a power of the largest number
  • PrimeGapsBridge PrimeGapsLib's gaps of at most 246 rest on Bombieri-Vinogradov; matching statements lets those results apply here
  • ParityBarrier Selberg's parity example; bombieri_asymptotic_sieve records that the conjecture alone does not get past it
  • MaierMatrix Maier's matrix method, which Friedlander and Granville adapted to show the full width fails

column_miss, level_of_distribution, level_mono, bombieri_vinogradov, elliott_halberstam, friedlander_granville, fixed_column_level, eh_bounded_gaps, geh_bounded_gaps, bombieri_asymptotic_sieve

Plan

Define the worst column miss for one width and the level-of-distribution property in RNS vocabulary (widths, survivor columns, fair share). Prove level_mono. State Bombieri-Vinogradov, Friedlander-Granville, the fixed-column record, Maynard's and Polymath8b's gap consequences and Bombieri's parity result as cited claims, and Elliott-Halberstam as a named open hypothesis. Check Axiom's PrimeGapsLib for its Bombieri-Vinogradov statement and match it, so PrimeGapsBridge can carry its results over.
